title: Do weighting, outcome-model, doubly robust and forest estimators fail at the same point as overlap goes?
question: As source-target divergence grows, does MAIC fail by variance and a linear outcome model by extrapolation bias at onsets that no single overlap statistic orders, and does a doubly robust estimator or a random forest fail later than both, on a continuous and a log odds ratio scale?
design: Gaussian covariate shift spaced evenly in log(1 + chi-squared), with modifier curvature varied at fixed divergence under common random numbers; unadjusted, MAIC, STC, augmented MAIC and a per-arm random forest; bias and variance onsets on a continuous and a binary scale. 36 cells, 1000 replicates each.
